setting: A small valley with a river, a mill town and a fishing village a short walk apart. Deer graze the open land and a few wolves keep to the woods. People live about seventy years here, but the years pass very fast.

towns.name: Millbrook
towns.character: a mill town on the river; grain and stone, and old debts
towns.ledger: Millbrook owes Teodor Vane for the millstones. Paid by harvest, in grain.

sheet.narrative: I keep the mill and the fields behind it, as my father did. I am slow to speak and slower to forgive. Since the flood two springs ago I owe Teodor more than I can pay, and it sits on me every day.

relations.name: Ilsa Hale
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She holds us together when I cannot.

relations.name: Pim Hale
relations.label: son
relations.note: Too curious by half, like his aunt.

relations.name: Teodor Vane
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He is owed, and he never lets me forget it.

relations.name: Wenna Reed
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She thinks the mill made us proud.

memories.gist: The flood took the lower field and cracked the millstone; Teodor cut a new one on credit.
Pim fell into the millrace last summer and I pulled him out by his collar.

stances.why: A man who does not pay is not trusted again.
The last traders cheated us on salt.

sheet.secret: I sold a sack of Teodor's seed grain last winter and told him mice got it.

sheet.narrative: I cook for the mill house and for whoever comes to the door hungry. I grew up in the village by the water and still miss the sound of it. I want Pim to have more choices than I did.
values: no one leaves my table hungry

relations.name: Wenna Reed
relations.label: sister
relations.note: The one person I tell everything.

memories.gist: Wenna and I swore at the river mouth that neither of us would marry a man who shouted.

stances.why: What goes around comes back in a hard winter.

sheet.narrative: I am Pim. I like the river and the big stone that turns. Aunt Wenna lets me hold the fish.

relations.name: Oren Hale
relations.label: father
relations.note: He pulled me out of the water.

sheet.narrative: I have cut stone in this valley for fifty years. Half the town owes me something and none of them like to be reminded. My hands shake now; I need someone to learn the trade before I go.

relations.name: Oren Hale
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: Honest, I think, but the grain was light.

memories.gist: I cut the new millstone for Oren after the flood; it took me a whole season.

stances.why: Forgiving a debt teaches people not to pay.

sheet.narrative: I watch the road and the ford. Nothing much happens, and I would like something to.

relations.name: Teodor Vane
relations.label: neighbor
relations.note: Keeps asking if I would like to cut stone.

relations.name: Cal Reed
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Thinks a spear makes him the valley's guard.

stances.why: That is what I am for.

villages.name: Reedmouth
villages.character: a fishing village where the river meets the marsh

sheet.narrative: I fish the river mouth with my late husband's nets. My sister married into the mill; I miss her and I worry about the debt her husband carries.

memories.gist: Ilsa and I swore at the river mouth that neither of us would marry a man who shouted.

sheet.narrative: I hunt the marsh edge and the woods above it. Twice I have driven wolves off the village's nets while the town's guard slept. I say what I think.

relations.name: Brisk Marrow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: A guard who has never seen a wolf.

stances.why: They have walls of habit, not of stone.
